title: Govt starts action plan to tackle urban flooding, heatwave risk - The Times of India
full_text:
Govt starts action plan to tackle urban flooding, heatwave risk
Officials discussed a coordinated framework covering preparation of detailed project reports, funding arrangements, capacity building, technical support and institutional mechanisms for implementation. The proposed measures will target all six municipal corporations and key towns in other urban local bodies.
Padhee directed officials to prepare a time-bound action plan defining responsibilities of different agencies. She suggested that the proposal be placed before the upcoming urban conclave to ensure wider stakeholder participation and consultation. Stressing the need for an integrated approach, she also called for coordination with other key agencies.
On heatwave preparedness, Padhee asked officials to identify urban hotspots requiring immediate intervention and develop a set of common measures that can be adopted across cities. She said guidelines should clearly mention immediate interventions as well as the funding sources available for their implementation.
Emphasising the need for visible outcomes, Padhee asked departments to ensure concrete relief measures are in place before next summer. She also advocated systematic planning of medium- and long-term interventions, including large-scale plantations and other nature-based solutions in coordination with the forest department.
The meeting also reviewed regulatory aspects such as building rules, bye-laws and planning provisions that could support climate resilience measures. Padhee proposed utilising the expertise of Odisha Urban Academy to provide structured training programmes for officials and technical personnel.

title: Odisha H&UD department holds high-level meeting on urban heatwave, flood preparedness and modernisation of storm-water drainage – ODISHA RAY - ODISHA RAY
full_text:
Bhubaneswar: The Odisha Housing & Urban Development department on Tuesday held a high-level meeting to deliberate on mitigation strategies and preparedness for urban heatwave and flooding, along with modernisation of storm-water drainage systems across major urban areas of the state. The meeting was chaired by Additional Chief Secretary, Housing & Urban Development department, Usha Padhee, at the 3rd Floor Conference Hall of Kharavela Bhawan, Bhubaneswar.
State Relief Commissioner (SRC) Rajesh Pravakar Patil, Director, Municipal Administration, Arindam Dakua, Commissioner, Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation, Chanchal Rana, Additional Secretary, H&UD Department, Rabindra Sahu, EIC, PHEO, Bilas Behera, EIC, OWSSB, Bhagyadhar Mohanty, and other senior officers were present.
Addressing the meeting, ACS Usha Padhee emphasised the need to bring all relevant stakeholders on board and develop a clear Action Plan with defined responsibilities and timelines. She suggested that the matter may also be taken up formally at the upcoming Urban Conclave to facilitate wider stakeholder participation and coordinated action.
On urban heatwave preparedness, Padhee called for identification of hotspots requiring immediate intervention in ULBs, along with a set of common interventions that can be undertaken across urban areas. She emphasised the need for clear guidelines indicating the measures that can be taken up immediately and the funding sources that may be utilised for their implementation.
Capacity building was identified as another important component of the proposed strategy.
Padhee suggested that the Odisha Urban Academy may be leveraged for structured training programmes for officials and technical personnel. She called for preparation of suitable training modules so that capacity-building activities can be taken up through the Academy.
With regard to storm-water management, Padhee directed the Urban Planning Section to take up the issue on priority. She proposed entering into an MoU for the purpose and suggested that, thereafter, the concerned section of OWSSB may facilitate engagement of a Project Management Consultant (PMC).
Padhee emphasised that immediate interventions should go hand in hand with medium- and long-term measures. She called for a clear focus on implementation, inter-agency coordination and delivery of tangible outcomes, with the objective of strengthening urban preparedness and resilience and providing visible relief to citizens before the next summer.
The meeting laid emphasis on translating the deliberations into a structured Action Plan covering priority interventions, stakeholder coordination, funding, technical support, capacity building and institutional mechanisms for implementation.This version positions the meeting as a strategic planning/way-forward meeting, rather than a review of past performance.
